title: What do we get when we add neighbouring triangular numbers?
description: The triangular numbers one, three, six, ten and fifteen are added in neighbouring pairs. The sums are four, nine, sixteen and twenty five, and a picture shows two triangles of dots fitting into a square.
teaching_notes: One idea: two neighbouring triangles of dots fit together into one square of dots. Watch for students who flip the small triangle the wrong way and leave a gap.

source: Figure it Out Q5 (Try This), p.8
video_script.why: The child adds neighbouring terms of the triangular numbers, as in the solved example, and uses a picture of dots to see why the sums form a new sequence.
video_script.substitution: The numbers are the triangular numbers instead of the even numbers.
video_script.anchor: two triangles of dots, one turned over, fitting into a square
video_script.payoff_line: Neighbouring triangular numbers add up to the square numbers, since two triangles of dots fit into a square

final_answer.value: 4, 9, 16, 25, ... the square numbers; two neighbouring triangles of dots fit together into a square
final_answer.spoken: the square numbers, since two triangles fit into a square

maths_rules: a triangle of 6 dots (rows 1, 2, 3) and a triangle of 3 dots (rows 1, 2) turned over fit into a 3 by 3 square of 9 dots
check: 1 + 3 = 4, a triangle of 3 dots and a triangle of 1 dot fit into a 2 by 2 square
video_script.design: The triangular numbers sit in a row. Neighbouring pairs are added. Then one pair of triangles of dots is slid together into a square.
